title: Ultra-processed food linked to early death
titleChinese: 食用超加工食品可能导致早逝
paragraphs: It’s good to enjoy food, but sometimes stories about the dangers of eating certain things can be hard to digest. I love to tuck into a pepperoni pizza or munch on a jam doughnut, even though I know the dangers that lurk in their ingredients. It’s clear that processed foods are not the most nutritious things; but there now comes a new threat - from ultra-processed foods.

Scientists have now discovered that eating these types of food - such as chicken nuggets, ice cream and breakfast cereals - have been linked to early death and poor health. This is the stuff that has been through more substantial industrial processing and often has long ingredient lists on the packet, including added preservatives, sweeteners or colour enhancers.

Knowing that your bowl of cornflakes could be bad for you might be hard to swallow, but two studies have shown that people eating more ultra-processed food had worse heart health. Dr Mathilde Touvier from the University of Paris, who conducted one of the studies, told the BBC: "The rapid and worldwide increasing consumption of ultra-processed foods, to the detriment of less processed foods, may drive a substantial burden of cardiovascular diseases in the next decades."

But it might not be completely necessary to change your diet just yet as there is still some uncertainty about the results of the study and questions still to answer. Kevin McConway, a professor of statistics at The Open University, told the BBC: "These studies do increase my confidence that there's something real behind these associations - but I'm still far from sure."

Maybe we should follow the advice of The US National Institutes of Health, which found that ultra-processed foods lead people to eat more and put on more weight. It suggests avoiding food containing ingredients you cannot pronounce or anything your grandmother would not recognise as food! The obvious thing to do seems to be to feast on more unprocessed foods, such as fruit, vegetables, fish, nuts and seeds, beans, lentils and wholegrains, often called a Mediterranean-style diet. After all, we are what we eat!

vocabulary.entry: hard to digest /hɑːd tu daɪˈdʒest/ 难以接受；难以理解（此处为比喻义）
vocabulary.example: The criticism from her friend was hard to digest.
vocabulary.translation: 来自朋友的批评让她难以接受。

vocabulary.entry: tuck into /tʌk ˈɪntu/ 大快朵颐；尽情享用
vocabulary.example: We tucked into a delicious meal at the new restaurant.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在那家新餐厅大快朵颐了一顿美食。

vocabulary.entry: munch on /mʌntʃ ɒn/ 津津有味地嚼；小口啃
vocabulary.example: She was munching on an apple while reading the newspaper.
vocabulary.translation: 她一边看报纸，一边津津有味地啃着苹果。

vocabulary.entry: lurk /lɜːk/ v. 潜藏；潜伏
vocabulary.example: Dangers lurk in the dark forest.
vocabulary.translation: 黑暗的森林中潜藏着危险。

vocabulary.entry: processed food /prəˈsesd fuːd/ 加工食品
vocabulary.example: Processed food is often high in salt and sugar.
vocabulary.translation: 加工食品通常含盐和糖量较高。

vocabulary.entry: ultra-processed food /ˌʌltrə prəˈsesd fuːd/ 超加工食品
vocabulary.example: Ultra-processed foods are convenient but not very healthy.
vocabulary.translation: 超加工食品很方便，但不太健康。

vocabulary.entry: be linked to /bi lɪŋkt tu/ 与……相关联；与……有联系
vocabulary.example: Smoking is linked to an increased risk of lung cancer.
vocabulary.translation: 吸烟与肺癌风险增加有关联。

vocabulary.entry: early death /ˈɜːli deθ/ 早逝；过早死亡
vocabulary.example: Poor living conditions are a factor in early death in some regions.
vocabulary.translation: 恶劣的生活条件是一些地区早逝的一个因素。

vocabulary.entry: substantial industrial processing /səbˈstænʃl ɪnˈdʌstriəl ˈprəʊsesɪŋ/ 复杂工业加工
vocabulary.example: This product undergoes substantial industrial processing before reaching consumers.
vocabulary.translation: 这款产品在送达消费者手中前经过了复杂的工业加工。

vocabulary.entry: preservative /prɪˈzɜːvətɪv/ n. 防腐剂
vocabulary.example: Preservatives are added to food to extend its shelf life.
vocabulary.translation: 防腐剂被添加到食物中以延长其保质期。

vocabulary.entry: sweetener /ˈswiːtnə(r)/ n. 甜味剂
vocabulary.example: Artificial sweeteners are often used in diet drinks.
vocabulary.translation: 人工甜味剂常被用于无糖饮料中。

vocabulary.entry: colour enhancer /ˈkʌlə ɪnˈhɑːnsə(r)/ 色素增强剂；着色剂
vocabulary.example: The colour enhancer in the candy makes it more attractive to children.
vocabulary.translation: 糖果中的色素增强剂让它对儿童更有吸引力。

vocabulary.entry: hard to swallow /hɑːd tu ˈswɒləʊ/ 难以接受；难以相信
vocabulary.example: The news of his resignation was hard to swallow.
vocabulary.translation: 他辞职的消息让人难以相信。

vocabulary.entry: consumption /kənˈsʌmpʃn/ n. 消费；消耗量
vocabulary.example: The consumption of fast food has increased dramatically in recent years.
vocabulary.translation: 近年来，快餐的消费量大幅增长。

vocabulary.entry: to the detriment of /tu ðə ˈdetrɪmənt ɒv/ 对……有害；损害……
vocabulary.example: He worked long hours to the detriment of his health.
vocabulary.translation: 他长时间工作，损害了自己的健康。

vocabulary.entry: cardiovascular disease /ˌkɑːdiəʊˈvæskjələr dɪˈziːz/ 心血管疾病
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动可以降低患心血管疾病的风险。

vocabulary.entry: uncertainty /ʌnˈsɜːtnti/ n. 不确定性；含糊不清
vocabulary.example: There is some uncertainty about the future of the project.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目的未来存在一些不确定性。

vocabulary.entry: put on weight /pʊt ɒn weɪt/ 增重；长胖
vocabulary.example: She put on a few kilos during the winter holiday.
vocabulary.translation: 她在寒假期间长胖了几公斤。

vocabulary.entry: unprocessed food /ʌnˈprəsesd fuːd/ 未加工食品
vocabulary.example: Unprocessed foods retain more natural nutrients.
vocabulary.translation: 未加工食品保留了更多天然营养成分。

vocabulary.entry: wholegrain /ˈhəʊlɡreɪn/ n. 全谷物
vocabulary.example: Wholegrain bread is healthier than white bread.
vocabulary.translation: 全谷物面包比白面包更健康。

vocabulary.entry: Mediterranean-style diet /ˌmedɪtəˈreɪniən staɪl ˈdaɪət/ 地中海式饮食
vocabulary.example: A Mediterranean-style diet is rich in vegetables, fish and olive oil.
vocabulary.translation: 地中海式饮食富含蔬菜、鱼类和橄榄油。

vocabulary.entry: we are what we eat /wi ɑː(r) wɒt wi iːt/ 我们吃什么，就是什么（指饮食影响健康和体质）
vocabulary.example: Eating fresh, healthy food is important - after all, we are what we eat.
vocabulary.translation: 吃新鲜健康的食物很重要——毕竟，我们吃什么，就是什么。

sentences.english: It’s good to enjoy food, but sometimes stories about the dangers of eating certain things can be hard to digest.
sentences.chinese: 享受美食感觉很好，但有时候关于某些食物存在危害的说法却让人难以接受。

sentences.english: I love to tuck into a pepperoni pizza or munch on a jam doughnut, even though I know the dangers that lurk in their ingredients.
sentences.chinese: 我喜欢大快朵颐意大利辣香肠披萨，或者津津有味地咀嚼果酱甜甜圈，尽管我知道它们的配料中潜藏着健康风险。

sentences.english: It’s clear that processed foods are not the most nutritious things; but there now comes a new threat - from ultra-processed foods.
sentences.chinese: 显然，加工食品并非最有营养的食物，但如今又出现了一种新的威胁——来自超加工食品。

sentences.english: Scientists have now discovered that eating these types of food - such as chicken nuggets, ice cream and breakfast cereals - have been linked to early death and poor health.
sentences.chinese: 科学家们现已发现，食用这类食物——比如鸡块、冰淇淋和早餐麦片——会导致早逝和健康状况不佳。

sentences.english: This is the stuff that has been through more substantial industrial processing and often has long ingredient lists on the packet, including added preservatives, sweeteners or colour enhancers.
sentences.chinese: 这类食物经过了更为复杂的工业加工，包装上的配料表通常很长，包含添加防腐剂、甜味剂或色素增强剂等成分。

sentences.english: Knowing that your bowl of cornflakes could be bad for you might be hard to swallow, but two studies have shown that people eating more ultra-processed food had worse heart health.
sentences.chinese: 得知自己吃的一碗玉米片可能对健康有害，或许会让人难以接受，但两项研究均表明，食用超加工食品较多的人，心脏健康状况更差。

sentences.english: Dr Mathilde Touvier from the University of Paris, who conducted one of the studies, told the BBC: "The rapid and worldwide increasing consumption of ultra-processed foods, to the detriment of less processed foods, may drive a substantial burden of cardiovascular diseases in the next decades."
sentences.chinese: 巴黎大学的玛蒂尔德·图维耶博士主持了其中一项研究，她向英国广播公司表示：“在全球范围内，超加工食品的消费量正快速增长，而低加工食品的消费却在减少，这可能会在未来几十年给心血管疾病带来沉重负担。”

sentences.english: But it might not be completely necessary to change your diet just yet as there is still some uncertainty about the results of the study and questions still to answer.
sentences.chinese: 不过，目前或许还没有必要彻底改变饮食习惯，因为研究结果仍存在一些不确定性，还有不少问题有待解答。

sentences.english: Kevin McConway, a professor of statistics at The Open University, told the BBC: "These studies do increase my confidence that there's something real behind these associations - but I'm still far from sure."
sentences.chinese: 开放大学的统计学教授凯文·麦康威向英国广播公司表示：“这些研究确实让我更相信，这些关联背后存在真实的影响——但我还远不能完全确定。”

sentences.english: Maybe we should follow the advice of The US National Institutes of Health, which found that ultra-processed foods lead people to eat more and put on more weight.
sentences.chinese: 或许我们应该听从美国国立卫生研究院的建议，该机构发现，超加工食品会让人吃得更多、越来越胖。

sentences.english: It suggests avoiding food containing ingredients you cannot pronounce or anything your grandmother would not recognise as food!
sentences.chinese: 建议避免食用含有你无法发音的配料的食物，或者你祖母认不出是食物的东西！

sentences.english: The obvious thing to do seems to be to feast on more unprocessed foods, such as fruit, vegetables, fish, nuts and seeds, beans, lentils and wholegrains, often called a Mediterranean-style diet.
sentences.chinese: 最明显的做法似乎是多享用未加工食品，比如水果、蔬菜、鱼类、坚果和籽类、豆类、小扁豆和全谷物——这类饮食通常被称为地中海式饮食。

sentences.english: After all, we are what we eat!
sentences.chinese: 毕竟，我们吃什么，就是什么！
